:::{#exr-negative-classification-complement}
#### Negative classification as a complement

In a [binary classification problem](#def-binary-classification) with $\scrC = \set{k_1, k_0}$,
show that when each observation is assigned a [class](#def-class) $Y \in \scrC$,
the [negative classification](#def-negative-classification) [event](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) $\negclass$
is the [complement](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-complement)
of the [positive classification](#def-positive-classification) event $\posclass$:
$\negclass = \neg \posclass$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-negative-classification-complement}

Because $\scrC = \set{k_1, k_0}$ with $\abs{\scrC} = 2$ (@def-binary-classification),
the [classes](#def-class) $k_1$ and $k_0$ are distinct,
so $Y \in \scrC$ equals $k_0$ if and only if $Y \neq k_1$:

$$
\ba
\negclass
&= \set{Y = k_0}
&& \text{(definition of negative classification)} \\
&= \set{Y \neq k_1}
&& \text{(since } Y \in \set{k_1, k_0} \text{ with } k_1 \neq k_0\text{)} \\
&= \neg \set{Y = k_1}
&& \text{(definition of complement)} \\
&= \neg \posclass
&& \text{(definition of positive classification)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-negative-classification-complement-exr}
:::
